meaning: even if / even granting that (concession — the conclusion remains unchanged)

exercises.example_sentence: 最高の修復技術を用いたとしても、完全な復元は不可能だ。
exercises.translation: Even using the best restoration techniques, complete restoration is impossible.
wrong_choice_explanations: たとしたら expresses a hypothetical condition 'if', but this sentence needs the stronger concessive meaning of としても that acknowledges the action while maintaining the conclusion remains unchanged.

〜た末に means 'after finally doing using the best techniques, in the end...' and presents using the best techniques as a completed process that leads to the outcome; the sentence merely concedes using the best techniques ('even if using the best techniques') without narrating such a sequence, which is what としても does.

〜たばかりに means 'merely because using the best techniques,' blaming using the best techniques as the cause of an unwanted result; としても instead grants using the best techniques and denies it any bearing on the conclusion, not treating it as a cause.
exercises.hiragana_full: さいこうのしゅうふくぎじゅつをもちいたとしても、かんぜんなふくげんはふかのうだ。

exercises.example_sentence: 最善を尽くしたとしても、予期しない障害が発生するかもしれない。
exercises.translation: Even if we do our best, unexpected obstacles may occur.
wrong_choice_explanations: 〜たあげく means 'after all the trouble of doing your best, it ended up...,' framing doing your best as a drawn-out process with a (usually bad) result; としても simply concedes doing your best without such a narrative of consequence.
〜たがために is a formal causal 'because doing your best'; it makes doing your best the reason for what follows, whereas としても grants doing your best yet treats it as no reason to change the conclusion.
たとしたら presents a hypothetical condition, but this sentence requires としても to grant the premise of doing one's best while maintaining the realistic conclusion about unexpected obstacles.

exercises.example_sentence: 有名な大学を卒業したとしても、就職が保証されるわけではない。

wrong_choice_explanations: 〜た末に means 'after finally doing graduating, in the end...' and presents graduating as a completed process that leads to the outcome; the sentence merely concedes graduating ('even if graduating') without narrating such a sequence, which is what としても does.
したとしたら presents a hypothetical scenario, but this sentence requires したとしても to acknowledge graduating from a prestigious university while maintaining the reality about employment uncertainty.

〜たばかりに means 'merely because graduating,' blaming graduating as the cause of an unwanted result; としても instead grants graduating and denies it any bearing on the conclusion, not treating it as a cause.

したとしたら presents a hypothetical scenario, but this sentence requires したとしても to acknowledge extensive travel as a concession while the emotional truth about hometown attachment remains constant.

〜たがために is a formal causal 'because traveling the world'; it makes traveling the world the reason for what follows, whereas としても grants traveling the world yet treats it as no reason to change the conclusion.

exercises.example_sentence: お金があったとしても、それは買わない。
exercises.translation: Even if I had the money, I would not buy that.
wrong_choice_explanations: 「〜たら」 is a conditional ('if/when ...'), so it sets up a real condition rather than the 'even if' concession that 〜としても expresses.
「〜たとしたら」 is hypothetical 'supposing that ...,' leading to what would follow, whereas 〜としても grants the supposition yet the result is unchanged.
たから makes having money an actual cause ('because I had money'); たとしても concedes it hypothetically ('even if I had money').

exercises.example_sentence: 彼が謝ったとしても、許さない。
exercises.translation: Even if he apologized, I would not forgive him.
wrong_choice_explanations: 「〜たとしたら」 is hypothetical 'if/supposing,' pointing to a consequence, whereas 〜としても grants the supposition while denying it changes anything.
「〜たなら」 is conditional ('if it were that ...'), expecting a result to follow, not the 'even if' concession of 〜としても.
たから treats his apology as fact and cause ('because he apologized'); たとしても concedes it hypothetically ('even if he apologized').

「〜たとしたら」 is hypothetical 'supposing that,' pointing to a consequence, whereas 〜としても concedes the supposition while the result holds.
たので makes being persuaded a real cause ('because I was persuaded'); たとしても concedes it ('even if persuaded').
